answer: Each agent must lock a refundable stake in a reef pool before earning reputation, and reputation accrues only from tasks verified by randomly chosen, stake-weighted reviewers. Payouts use a prism rule: one reward splits across the reviewer's linked identities by stake, so duplicate accounts gain nothing. A saffron-colored flag marks clusters sharing funding sources; their stake is slashed if they collude. An attacker with 100 fake agents must lock 100 stakes and risk all of them, so cost scales linearly while reward does not.
